title: Protocol for single-cell isolation and genome amplification of environmental microbial eukaryotes for genomic analysis
protocol: Put on laboratory gloves.
Disinfect the gloves.
Using collection gear, place an aliquot of the environment in which the taxa of interest are present into sterile storage labware.
Bring the sample to the laboratory.
Keep the sample in its original conditions.
Examine the sample under the microscope and determine your target environmental microbial eukaryote (EME) concentration using a hemocytometer.
Take pictures of the target EME at small and high magnification.
Take three 500 μL aliquots of the sample and put each in a pre-sterilized 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Place the first aliquot on ice for 15–30 min, then move to -20°C for 30 min, and finally to -80°C for 24 h–168 h.
Add sterile glycerol to the second aliquot dropwise to achieve a final concentration of 30%, gently pipette 2–5 times without vortexing or shaking, place on ice, and transfer to -80°C for 24 h–168 h.
Place the third aliquot at -80°C in a pre-chilled container for 24 h–168 h.
Thaw all three aliquots simultaneously at 20°C–21°C or on ice if originally collected below 15°C.
Calculate the target EME concentration using a hemocytometer after thawing.
Compare the post-thaw concentration with the pre-freezing concentration.
If the post-thaw concentration is less than 20% of the original, the freezing method is not suitable for storage and transportation.
Use the freezing method if the post-thaw concentration remains within 20% variation from the original sample.
Store samples at -80°C or transport on dry ice using a suitable freezing method.
If no suitable method is found, store 4°C-collected samples at 4°C and transport them on ice.
Transport 20°C–21°C collected samples at 20°C–21°C.
Process 20°C–21°C samples as quickly as possible or enrich for the EME.
If the target EME concentration in your sample is less than 103/mL and the environment is rich in other organisms, proceed to point b.
If the target EME concentration is above 103/mL, collect enough volume of sample to amount to 106–1024 total target EME and store as determined to be optimal in step 2.
Use the appropriate filtration system (e.g., Cell strainers) to filter out the most abundant non-target population by size.
Avoid vacuum filtration; use gravity to filter out larger and smaller populations.
Pause point: The next step can be done on the first day of collection or at a later date.
Target EME operational taxonomic unit identification and abundance estimation via ribosomal DNA genes.
Dissolve a sample aliquot of 50–100 μL in 1 mL of Milli-Q 0.1–0.2 μM filter-sterilized water.
If sample amount is restricted or expected concentration of the target is very high (106/mL or more), use a 2 μL in 100 μL of water dilution.
Boil for 2 min to release the DNA into solution.
Cool on ice.
Prepare sufficient PCR master mix for each rDNA gene primer-pair in triplicate.
Keep the PCR master mix on ice.
Aliquot 7 μL of master mix into separate thin-wall 200 μL tubes or appropriate plates.
Add 1 μL of boiled and chilled DNA to each well/tube.
Add 1 μL of 10 μM each primer from each primer pair to each reaction.
Prepare one NGS Illumina or PacBio library per primer pair using manufacturer instructions.
Follow sequencing instructions for rDNA analysis.
Sterilize the fluid lines of the cell sorter using a 10% Bleach solution prepared with a 0.2 μM filtration system.
Run the sterilization process through the lines for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Use between 500 mL to 700 mL bleach for the fluid lines sterilization.
Store the remaining bleach in a sterile container for cleaning surfaces.
Prepare 2000 mL of autoclave Milli-Q water.
Prepare 1000 mL of filter-sterilized Milli-Q water.
Use autoclaved H2O to rinse the tank from bleach three times with 500 mL each time.
Run the 1000 mL filter-sterilized H2O through the fluid lines that have been sterilized with bleach.
Rinse until the lines dry out completely.
Remove the tip and continue until no water comes out.
Place the clean tank for single-cell sheath fluid in the UV hood opened with the lid inside out.
Turn on UV lamp for overnight UV-decontamination.
UV-sterilize the sorting area if enclosed.
Spray the sorting area with sterile 70% Ethanol and let dry.
Wipe the plates clean with 70% ethanol if salt residues are present.
Prepare 3–5 L of 0.2 μM filter-sterilized PBS at 1× or 0.5× concentration from a non-sterile 10× stock solution.
Filter-sterilize sea or ocean water for marine organisms, performing multiple filtrations if necessary.
Final filtration should be 0.2 μM sterile filter for organisms larger than 1 μm or use 0.01 μm filtration systems for ultra-small organisms.
Sonicate the sorting tip in 1% Alconox solution at medium power for 5 min.
Check fluid movement through the tip using a 3 mL–10 mL syringe with sterile water or sheath-fluid.
Hold the tip with sterile forceps; install into metal threaded holder if hard to hold.
Close the UV-sterilized tank in the hood.
Zero tare with an empty tank on the scale.
Pour filter-sterilized PBS sheath fluid into the tank inside the hood.
Connect lines to the sheath and waste tanks.
Record the weight of the full tank for later use.
Turn on air and vacuum pump, check pressure: Sheath tank should be 15 psi, waste tank 10–15 Hg.
Adjust sample pressure to 16 using the knobs on the far-right side.
Adjust sheath pressure to 16.8 using the knobs on the far-right side.
Turn on electronics (red switch under the Influx table top).
Turn on computer and laser(s) – 488 nm: switch & key on control box when Ready light is on.
Increase laser power to 98% in the screen if necessary.
Rinse briefly without a tip to fill fluid lines, ensuring not to overflow the receptacle basin.
Replace tip after rinsing.
Run with tip in place for a couple of minutes.
Immerse tip into 70% EtOH.
Turn off Run when the tip is immersed.
Purge lines to de-bubble using Pulse button.
Flick lines during purging.
Ensure tip stays immersed to prevent air from being pulled in.
Restart de-bubbling if air enters the system.
Stop purge and press Run, then immediately remove the orange cap.
Absorb droplets on the outside of the tip using the corner of a wipe.
Turn on Illum – button on the top part of the screen.
Check stream alignment relative to the drain cup and three pinholes.
Adjust position of the stream and camera using brass knobs if necessary.
Lower tip so that its shadow is just visible on top of the pinhole camera screen.
Center stream over the pinholes and bring edges into focus.
Check that the stream is centered in the drain cup.
Take a 1-h break after initial setup.
Check that plate voltage is shut off.
Clean plates with sterile alcohol wipe.
Close the plates.
Turn on Plates.
Value should be ≈ 3.6 V ± 0.1 (left positive, right negative).
Close stream-area cover and open laser shutters: Pull knob on the far-left side and wave your finger in front of the camera window.
Set laser power to desired level.
Use laser optics stages knobs to place laser beam on the stream over the top pinhole.
Set the arrow (in the middle top window) at the bottom of the cut-off droplet.
Check that sort area is clear.
Start Spigot software & open desired configuration file.
In the SORT menu choose a window with pre-set sorting parameters (fluorescence and size): e.g., 488 vs FSC.
Inactivate other sorting windows if active from before.
Let instrument stabilize for at least 1 h.
Check if the arrow is still pointing to the same place as before stabilizing.
Bring calibration beads relevant to the target organism size.
Vortex the beads to de-clump.
Dilute the beads according to manufacturer instructions.
Place the tube with diluted beads in the sample holder.
Press Sample and Boost until signals appear on the screen.
Stop Boost, keep Sample.
Using laser optics stage knobs, maximize fluorescence.
Adjust dots position for tight grouping in the higher part of the sorting window.
Set beads group in far-left side if sorting larger cells or far-right top corner if sorting smaller cells.
Stop Sample.
Remove tube with calibration beads and set aside.
Turn on Backflush to clear beads from sample line.
Click on “Sort Config” and adjust droplet frequency and piezo.
Move camera up and down the droplet stream using the silver knob.
Check deflection (left).
Turn on Flash charge, adjust Piezo Amplitude value.
Test streams should be steady when toggling flash on and off.
Note droplet break-off image – it should stay the same, if not, count again droplet position: break-off point, 4 droplets down, 5 droplets up, laser (top of the stream at the tip end).
Approximate drop delay (18–20) using Spigot – press Count.
Turn on microscope fluorescent light to warm up.
Calibrate drop delay by sorting 5 × 5 matrix (glass slide) and counting (green) beads (2 μm) on fluorescent scope.
Press Sample; Boost until signals (enough dots on the screen) appear.
Stop Boost. keep Sample.
Choose “Calibration Slide” in the Sorted Sample Container.
Press Sort ready.
After sorting onto the slide Stop Sample.
View calibration slide under fluorescent light on the microscope using 10× objective.
Count the beads in several droplets, starting with the middle one, then the higher and the lower (should be ± 5 beads).
Choose the correct drop position from the slide (max number of beads).
Press on slide layout table the drop position with the best bead count.
Software will adjust the droplet interval.
Verify calibration 2 times at least.
Backflush between beads and between samples with sheath fluid.
Use 10% sterile Bleach in the sample line if beads or sample are too sticky, for a few minutes, followed by backflush.
Increase or decrease sample pressure based on the stream in the Pinhole screen, not the Total Rate.
Do not exceed 400 events per second; dilute samples to obtain around 100 events per second.
Dilute very small-volume samples further and reduce to minimum possible events per second to minimize losses.
Practice with various bead dilutions prior to sorting.
Choose the Sorted Sample Container (tube or 384-well plate) for target enrichment and single or multiple-cell 384-well plates.
Calibrate the stream position in the well.
Determine the tube angle for obtaining the sorted droplet at the desired location.
Mark a few wells in column 1 of the calibration 384-well plate for the top of the 0.3 μL volume.
Sort clean sheath fluid into each well of column 2 for 500–1000 'imaginary' events using the sorting software.
Temporarily move the laser beam into the noise area of the stream during calibration.
Return the laser beam to the correct droplet position when sorting real events.
Inspect the sorted fluid drop visually.
Increase or decrease offset on the x-axis and/or y-axis if the drop is too far off the well bottom.
Adjust the position using offsets: increase the number to shift the drop as desired, starting with one axis only.
Repeat the offset establishment process for columns 11 and 22.
Choose a value that positions the droplet around the bottom of the well, not higher than the 300 nL mark for all three columns.
Select a desired sorting window, such as 488 vs FSC or FSC vs SSC.
Close other opened/active windows.
Stain the sample with Syto-9 (excited at 488 nm) for DNA and another dye if needed, selecting correct laser/filter for each type of dye.
Dilute the sample with sterile sheath-fluid or sterile water if necessary.
Place the sample tube into the sample tube holder until it clicks in place.
Run the sample and boost until the cell population starts to appear in the active window.
Stop boosting, keep the sample.
Gate each cell population.
Choose the populations wanted to be sorted.
Perform an exploratory sort from each gate into a tube if the population of interest is not known.
Sort until a 2–5 μL droplet appears on the tube wall.
Examine under the microscope.
Sort each gate into three separate wells (500 events) and perform rDNA qPCR using lysis and neutralization buffer if the organism's shape is unknown.
If more than one primer pair is intended to be used, perform a brief MDA followed by steps 25 and 26 after MDA amplification.
Follow available NGS or Sanger sequencing for OTU identification.
Sort the desired organisms into a sterile tube filled with 1–2 mL of sterile sheath fluid.
Verify under the microscope that the desired organism was sorted and the cleanliness of the enrichment.
Insert a single-cell clean (10–15 min UV sterilized in the Stratalinker 2400) 384-well Bio Rad qPCR clear plate into the plate holder.
Sort sheath fluid using column 2.
Set the event to the maximum of the multi-cell sort (e.g., 100 events if sorting 100 cells).
Use column 3 to sort multiple-cell sorts for positive controls (e.g., 10-cells, 50-cells, or 100-cells).
For easy-to-lyse cells, use 10-cells.
For small genomes from relatively clean populations, increase the number of multiple-cells sorted into one well.
After single-cell lysis, proceed directly to amplified NGS library creation (increase cycle to 21 cycles) if genome amplification is not required.
Use the rest of the wells for single-cell sorting, except columns 23 and 24 which are reserved for later use in the next step.
Seal the plate with sterile aluminum foil after sorting is complete.
Place the sealed plate on dry ice in a Styrofoam box for transportation to the −80°C freezer for long-term storage.
Record weight on scale to determine consumed and remaining sheath fluid volume.
Add 2 mL of 10% bleach to sample tube and sample for 10 min.
Remove bleach tube and backflush for 1 min.
Add 2 mL of filter-sterilized H2O to sample tube and sample for 5 min.
Close laser shutter(s) and take off run.
Detach sheath lines, vent sheath tank, and dispose of excess sheath fluid down drain.
Add 500 mL of filter-sterilized Milli-Q H2O to the sheath tank used for bleaching the lines and connect fluid and pressure lines to sheath tank and pressurize.
Put the waste basin beneath tip, push rinse and backflush sample line (back-flushing will continue until fluid is gone and air is flowing through the tubing).
Continue until no events are visible and the lines are dry.
Shut off lasers.
UV-sterilize the sort area or wipe clean with 70% alcohol.
Remove tip and run for 5 min until no trace of water comes out.
Turn off run.
Shut down software & computer.
Shut off electronics.
Shut off vacuum pump & pressurized air.
Disconnect the waste tank and add bleach to final conc. of 10% by volume, and let sit for at least 15 min before disposing into the sink.
Rinse with tap water and set to dry.
UV-treat plasticware and stock solutions.
Wipe clean H2Osc and Stop Solution tubes with 15% bleach, followed by 70% sterile isopropanol.
Thaw H2Osc and Stop Solution tubes either in the hood with UV light on or in the Stratagene UV Stratalinker 2400 for 30 minutes.
Transfer 1 mL of H2Osc and 500 μL of the Stop Solution into two separate, new 1.5 mL clear DNAase, RNAase sterile Eppendorf tubes inside a clean hood.
Wipe clean a new bag of 1.5 mL clear Eppendorf tubes with sterile gloves in the clean hood.
Remove and UV sterilize 10–20 tubes for 1 hour on Stratagene UV Stratalinker 2400 along with components from step 12.
UV-treat the 384 well LabCyte plate (source plate for ECHO525) with clear seal for 30 to 60 minutes if using the LabCyte ECHO525 for reagent transfer.
Save UV-treated tubes in a sterile container or wrap them in aluminum foil and leave in the hood.
Prepare stock DLB buffer by adding 500 μL of the H2Osc (1-h UV-ed water) to the pellet in the supplied tube.
Vortex and spin down the prepared stock DLB buffer.
Add 200 μL of buffer DLB to empty new (not UV-treated) 1.5 mL clear DNAase, RNAase free sterile Eppendorf tubes.
Add 18 μL of DDT to the buffer DLB in the Eppendorf tubes.
Add 200 μL of UV-treated H2Osc to the mixture in the Eppendorf tubes.
Dispense 1 μL of Lysis buffer on pH strip; confirm pH is between 12-14.
UV sterilize Lysis buffer for 1 h in Stratagene UV Stratalinker 2400 on aluminum foil.
Dispense 1 μL of Stop buffer onto the Lysis droplet to neutralize pH.
Reconstitute SYTO-13 dye with UV-treated H2O in a 1:120 dilution.
Wrap the prepared SYTO-13 solution in aluminum foil and keep it in the hood.
Prepare MDA reaction mix in UV-treated Eppendorf tubes.
Keep the MDA reaction mix on a sterile cold block or at 4°C wrapped in aluminum foil until ready for use.
Add 50 μL of Lysis buffer to each of 8 wells in a UV-treated LabCyte plate.
Add 50 μL of Stop buffer to each of 4 wells in the same UV-treated LabCyte plate.
Seal the LabCyte plate with clear seal.
Centrifuge the source plate at 1548 × g for 3 minutes.
Centrifuge the destination plate next to ECHO525 machine for 2 minutes.
Create a new file for dispensing Lysis buffer each time it is needed.
Double-click on Echo Liquid Handler and ensure all buttons are green in diagnostic mode.
Double-click on Echo Plate Reformat, click connect, and open new file.
Choose the plate format as 384PP_AQ_BP (pre-calibrated).
Select BioRad384 (black lettering) as the destination plate format.
In mapping mode, choose custom settings and OK.
Pick the wells from the source plate that will be used.
Treat selected wells as identical well content.
Choose the wells on the destination plate to use.
Add regions for Sample, Negative control, and Positive control.
Set droplet volume to 500 nL.
Ensure offset is at (0,0).
Save file with name indicating solution type and date.
Create STOP buffer plate format using same steps as Lysis Plate file.
Change STOP buffer droplet volume to 250 nL.
Open the prepared file for dispensing.
Press run arrow (blue) to start process.
Insert source plate into lower holder, ensuring it rests firmly against the corner.
Press OK.
Insert destination plate into the upper plate holder.
Press OK.
Remove both plates from the ECHO plate holder after dispensing is completed.
Cover both plates with clear seal.
Centrifuge destination plate with Lysis buffer at 3000 rpm for 1 min.
Incubate destination plate at RT for 1–2 minutes (3 minutes total reaction time).
Use ECHO525 to dispense 250 nL Stop buffer into destination plate.
Open the file for Stop buffer dispensing created in point d.
Repeat the same steps as for the Lysis file (point e, f, g).
Return the destination plate to the clean hood for MDA reaction manual dispensing.
Wipe clean the plate.
Proceed to adding 3 μL MDA reaction mix to each well with Lysis + Stop solution without touching the plate wells with the tip.
Bring the 384-well plate with single cells from the −80°C storage.
Centrifuge briefly for 2 min at 3000 rpm in a Swing-bucket rotor benchtop refrigerated centrifuge set at 4°C–10°C.
Wipe clean the plate and bring it into the clean hood.
Add 1 μL of UV-treated Lysis buffer without touching the wells' plastic with the pipette tip.
Touch gently the drop on the upper side of the well to avoid cross-contamination.
Tap gently the plate to help the drop slide down into the well.
Cover the plate immediately with a sterile cover and centrifuge at 3000 rpm for 1 min.
Verify that each well has Lysis buffer covering the bottom of the well evenly.
Wipe the surface of the plate clean and return to the hood.
Incubate for 3 min in the hood, making sure the drop is on the bottom and covers evenly the sort area.
Remove the cover carefully as not to create any amount of aerosol.
Add 0.5 μL of UV-treated STOP buffer to neutralize the Lysis.
Cover with a sterile cover and centrifuge at 3000 rpm for 1 min.
Wipe clean the surface of the plate and return to the hood.
Dispense 6 μL of the MDA reaction mix without touching the plate with the tip.
Tap the plate lightly to allow the reaction mix to slide to the bottom of the well.
Cover the plate with an optically clear seal for the real-time Bio-Rad thermocycler.
Seal manually, except for the last two columns (23 and 24).
Centrifuge the destination plate at 2000 rpm for 2 min.
Lift the right side of the clear seal carefully to avoid exposing the rest of the wells to air.
Add 1 μL of 50–5000 femtogram purified DNA into the positive control wells (column 23) outside the clean hood.
Seal the tape fully before placing the plate in the Bio-Rad CFX384 Real-time thermocycler.
Incubate at 29°C–30°C for 1.5–4 h.
Add a read step every 10 minutes.
Include a heat kill step at the end (65°C for 10 min).
Stop the run if Negative control curves show in more than 2 wells.
Stop the run if more than 50% of the single-cell wells are in the logarithmic phase of amplification.
Avoid reaching the amplification curve plateau to minimize bias.
Continue incubation until 50% or more of the single-cell wells show amplification for larger genomes.
Do not exceed 4 h total incubation time.
For genomes between 10 Mb and 30 Mb, incubate for 2.5–3 hours.
Prepare 10× MDA reaction buffer with the final concentration of 400 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 100 mM MgCl2, 500 mM KCl, 50 mM (NH4)2SO4, and 20 mM DTT.
Filter sterilize the MDA reaction buffer using a 0.1 μm filter.
Aliquot 1 mL of the filtered MDA reaction buffer into screw cap sterile tubes that are DNA, RNA, and DNase, RNase free.
Store the aliquoted MDA reaction buffer at -20°C.
Filter Fisher ddH2O molecular grade water with a 0.2 or 0.1 μm sterile filter system.
UV-sterilize the bottle of filtered water for 1–3 h in the hood.
Aliquot 1 mL × 50 of the filtered water into 1.5 mL clear DNAase, RNAase sterile Eppendorf tubes in a clean hood.
Place the aliquots on aluminum foil and UV sterilize for 3 h using Stratagene UV Stratalinker 2400.
Store the sterilized water at -20°C.
Dissolve random hexamers from IDT to 500 mM concentration using the UV-sterilized water in a clean environment.
Aliquot the hexamers into 1.5 mL clear tubes, with 1 mL per tube.
Place four tubes on aluminum foil and transport them to Stratagene UV Stratalinker 2400.
UV sterilize each tube for 0.5 h, 1.5 h, 3 h, and 6 h respectively.
Store the UV-treated hexamer tubes at -20°C after each time point.
Dilute each UV-treated tube to 500 μM concentration using the UV-sterilized water from step one.
Perform a test MDA to establish optimal UV sterilization times for each batch of IDT hexamers, utilizing negative and positive control columns as specified.
UV-treat the rest of the tubes with the 500 mM hexamer aliquots.
Store the UV-treated tubes at −20°C.
Dilute one tube at a time to 500 μM with UV-treated H2O.
Aliquot 1 mL into 1.5 mL UV-sterilized tubes.
Wipe clean a new bag of 1.5 mL clear Eppendorf tubes in the clean hood.
Remove 10–20 tubes and close them inside the hood wearing sterile gloves.
Place the tubes on aluminum foil and UV-sterilize for 1 h using Stratagene UV Stratalinker 2400.
Prepare concentrated 500 mM KOH solutions in the clean hood using UV-treated water.
Aliquot into sterile screw cap tubes and store at −20°C.
Prepare concentrated 500 mM HCl solutions in the clean hood using UV-treated water.
Aliquot into sterile screw cap tubes and store at −20°C.
Aliquot 99.9% pure DMSO into dark ultra-pure (BioPure) 1.5 mL tubes.
Store the DMSO aliquots at −20°C.
Prepare stock DLB buffer by adding 500 μL UV-treated H2O to 400 μL KOH (500 mM).
UV sterilize for 30 min in Stratagene UV Stratalinker 2400 on aluminum foil.
Prepare STOP buffer by adding 400 μL HCl (500 mM) to 500 μL of UV-treated H2O.
Prepare Lysis Buffer by first adding 200 μL buffer DLB to a new empty tube.
Add 18 μL DTT and finally add 200 μL UV-treated H2O to the tube.
Dispense 1 μL of Lysis buffer on a pH strip to confirm the pH, which should be between 12 and 14.
Dispense 1 μL of Stop buffer onto the Lysis droplet to neutralize its pH.
Aliquot 120 μL of UV-treated H2O in a new clear 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
UV sterilize the aliquoted water, along with the Lysis and Stop buffers for 1 hour using a Stratagene UV Stratalinker 2400 on aluminum foil.
Place SYTO-13 in the dark at 20°C to 21°C one hour prior to use.
Prepare the MDA reaction in two clear 1.5 mL BioPure Eppendorf tubes, each containing 1 mL of the reaction mix.

UV treat the following items for 30 minutes to 1 hour prior to use: a 1.5 mL tube with the MDA reaction mix on aluminum foil placed on -20°C frozen packets; one 125 μL tip box and one 12.5 μL tip box, both opened.
Reconfirm the pH for Lysis and Stop buffer after UV-treatment as described above.
Make a 1:120 dilution of SYTO-13 dye in 120 μL UV-treated H2O.
Add 1 μL of the diluted SYTO-13 to each 1 mL tube with the UV-ed MDA reaction mix.
Keep the reaction mix on a sterile cold block or at 4°C until ready for use.
Centrifuge the 384-well plate briefly at 3000 rpm in a pre-chilled centrifuge.
Wipe clean the centrifuged plate and bring into the hood.
Add 1 μL of UV-treated lysis buffer to each well gently without touching the walls.
Tap the plate gently to ensure drops slide down from the top.
Cover the plate with a sterile cover and centrifuge for 1 min at 3000 rpm.
Verify that the lysis buffer covers the bottom evenly in each well.
Incubate the plate for 3 minutes in the hood.
Remove the cover carefully to avoid creating aerosol.
Add 1 μL of UV-treated STOP buffer to neutralize Lysis.
Cover with a sterile cover and centrifuge at 3000 rpm for 1 min.
Wipe clean the surface of the plate and return it to the hood.
Dispense 5 μL of MDA reaction mix without touching the plate with the pipette tip.
Tap lightly on the plate to allow the reaction mix to slide to the bottom of the well, ensuring no drops remain at the top of the wells.
Cover the plate with an optically clear seal for the real-time Bio-Rad thermocycler.
Manually seal the plate except for the last 2 columns (columns 23 and 24).
Centrifuge the plate at 2000 rpm for 2 min.
Carefully lift the right-side of the clear seal to avoid exposing other wells to air.
Add 1 μL of purified DNA into the positive control wells (column 24) outside the clean hood.
Seal the cover fully.
Remove side tabs before placing the plate in the Bio-Rad CFX384 Real-time thermocycler.
Incubate at 29°C–30°C for 4 h–16 h.
Add a read step every 10 minutes during incubation.
Include a heat kill step of 10 min at 65°C at the end of the reaction.
Stop the run if negative control curves show in more than 2 wells.
Stop the run if more than 50% of sorted single-cells are in logarithmic phase amplification.
Continue incubation until 50% or more of single-cell wells show amplification for genomes larger than 10 Mb.
Denature the amplified plate for 10 min at 65°C.
Store the MDA amplified plate at −20°C.
Filter sterilize and UV-treat a Tween 20 detergent stock solution for 3-16 hours in a clear bottle from the filter-system in the hood.
Aliquot the treated Tween 20 solution and store at -20°C for long-term storage.
Prepare a Tween 20 solution with a concentration that will result in 0.3% final concentration after added to the Lysis buffer.
UV-treat the stock solution along with water tubes.
Prepare a Proteinase K stock solution of maximum concentration in UV-treated water.
Filter sterilize the Proteinase K solution.
Aliquot 1 ml of the treated Proteinase K solution into 1.5 ml tubes, similar to the water above.
UV-treat for 30 minutes on cold packs in the sterile water bath.
Add UV-treated Proteinase K to the Lysis solution just prior to dispensing into wells with single-cells after the Lysis solution was UV-treated.
Wipe clean the hood with 15% bleach.
Bring rDNA primers into the clean hood.
Spin down and dissolve rDNA primers to a 100 μM stock concentration using UV-treated H2O.
Leave dissolved primers at 20°C–21°C for several hours.
Vortex briefly and spin down the primers again after leaving them at room temperature.
Freeze the primer solution at −20°C for 16–18 h.
Prepare a 10 μM working solution of each primer using UV-treated H2O.
Mix the primer solution up and down 10 times.
Store the primer solution at −20°C if not used immediately.
Retrieve MDA plate from −20°C freezer.
Centrifuge the MDA plate at 3000 rpm for five minutes.
Wipe clean the centrifuged MDA plate.
Add 15 μL of UV-treated H2O to the MDA amplified single-cell gDNA.
Mix the contents up and down 25 times or more using an automated multichannel pipette with thin tips.
Add 10 μL UV-treated water to the MDA gDNA plate.
Seal the plate with aluminum foil and freeze for 2 hours or longer at -20°C.
Thaw the plate by spinning at 2000 rpm for 5 minutes on a swing bucket rotor.
Place the plate on a horizontal mixer and vigorously mix at 1000 rpm for 15 minutes.
Centrifuge the plate again at 3000 rpm for 5 minutes.
Freeze the plate once more after removal of aluminum foil by spinning down.
Repeat the freeze-thaw and mixing cycles three times in total.
Aliquot 1 μL of the homogenized gDNA into a new 384-well clear plate, avoiding wall contact.
UV-treat the new plate for 10 minutes in the Stratagene UV Stratalinker 2400.
Cover the treated plate with optically clear film.
Aliquot gDNA from the MDA plate into PCR plates using a robotic or multi-dispense system if amplifying more than one region of rDNA simultaneously.
Seal the PCR plates with aluminum foil covers after aliquoting.
Store the sealed PCR plates at -20°C until needed for qPCR.
Select wells from the MDA plate that amplified well based on the examination of the amplification graph.
Record Cq values for each selected well.
Aliquot from the wells that have a positive Cq value.
Keep a record of which well was transferred to where.
Thaw the KAPA SybrFast qPCR 2× master mix in its original box or drawer.
Prepare the qPCR reaction mix in the clean hood with the lights off.
Multiply the amount of reagent required by the number of wells needed +2 or one column if doing a whole plate.
Add 9 μL of qPCR reaction mix to each well of the qPCR plate.
Add 1 μL of homogenized gDNA to each well of the qPCR plate.
Centrifuge the PCR plate at 2000 rpm for 5 minutes.
Remove side tabs before placing the PCR plate in the BioRad CFX384 Real-time machine.
Run the corresponding protocol that has optimal settings for the primers used.
Dilute the sequencing primer(s) as instructed for Sanger sequencing kit and protocol used.
Prepare one 96-well plate or tubes that fit any available thermocycler.
Prepare another plate or tubes that respond to the requirements of the sequencing technology adapted at your core facility or lab.
Use PacBio or other long read sequencing technology for NGS, e.g., 500 bp at least, to avoid assembly.
Follow standard library preparation instructions and proceed with sequencing.
Select wells for Sanger Sequencing based on the melting curves from qPCR results.
Choose wells that show a sharp peak in the melting curve.
Disregard wells with peaks that have a left shoulder.
Exclude wells with double peaks.
Wells with peaks having a right shoulder are likely to show high molecular weight smears.
Wells with round wide peaks are acceptable but not optimal for Sanger sequencing.
Spin down the qPCR plate at 3000g for 5 minutes.
Dispense 2 μL of ExoSap-IT into all wells in a new 96-well plate.
Transfer 5 μL of selected qPCR rDNA fragment to each well containing ExoSap-IT.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Inactivate by heating to 80°C for 15 minutes.
Cool down the plate to 4°C after inactivation.
Seal with aluminum foil if not using immediately for sequencing.
Freeze sealed plates at -20°C.
Transfer 5 μL of the treated reaction to a plate suitable for Sanger sequencing core facility.
Add forward or reverse primer to the ExoSap-IT-treated fragments.
Download software for analysis of rDNA Sequencing Results.
Download the appropriate module from DNASTAR Navigator.
Unzip results sent from the Core Sequencing Facility.
Use Sequencher to estimate sequence quality and trim low-quality ends.
Align highly similar sequences using Sequencher for fast screening of large batches.
Use BioEdit to view chromatographic traces in cases of nucleotide ambiguity or low-quality score.
Identify if low quality score is due to multiple sequences, lack of sequence, or high gDNA background using BioEdit.
When multiple sequencing happens and assuming all previous steps were followed correctly, consider a long-read NGS or short-read NGS + rDNA gene assembly for distinguishing between these rDNA.
Use the SeqMan Ultra module from DNASTAR package for Sanger and NGS read analysis.
Upload FASTA files to one of the software packages described above.
Analyze quality score and length using the uploaded software.
Trim low-quality ends if necessary.
Export trimmed sequences with high quality (at least 50% for long sequences or at least 70% for short sequences).
Arrange trimmed sequences in a FASTA file.
